common.statistic_default: Per half: per day, the mean over that day's trades of the measured quantity; day-equal mean; day-clustered t (df = days - 1).

common.power: Outcome-blind count step first: trades and days per half, and a projected MDE from the dispersion of the CONTROL leg only; floors per half >= 300 trades and >= 20 days, MDE <= the lift bar, else UNDERPOWERED with no outcome read.
common.fail_rule: FAIL: t <= -2 in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound of the lift below the bar in both halves. Otherwise not passed = UNDERPOWERED.

common.multiplicity: Eight studies registered together on 2026-10-23 (the 'untested categories' batch). Each has ONE primary; a family-wise reading is printed: a primary counts as a batch PASS only with t >= 2.73 (Bonferroni 0.05/8, two-sided, normal approx) in both halves; t >= 2 in both halves without that is reported as 'PASS (single-test), not batch-robust'.
amended: (C1) Cross-sectional studies (no control leg): the power MDE comes from a PLACEBO - a seeded random set of the same size as the long set each day (seed '<study>-placebo') minus the all-eligible mean; MDE = (t 2.0 + 0.84) x SD(day placebo LIFT) / sqrt(days). The placebo is outcome-free with respect to the signal.

(C2) No eligibility test may use a bar after entry. Exit price = the close of the last bar at or before the exit minute; a name lacking the exit-minute bar is NOT skipped. A name lacking its entry bar is skipped (counted) - the entry bar is known at entry.
(C3) Confirmation window for fresh-fetch studies: 2026-01-14 .. 2026-04-24 (the warehouse_confirm dates), fetched ONLY after a PASS, never before; no study's scored halves may include it.
(C4) Every fetch logs symbols dropped by rate-limit errors (429) after retries; a half with any unrecovered drop is refused (rerun the fetch).

Universe fact (declared): the warehouse is NOT book-like - it is every liquid name (prior-day raw close >= $10, 20-day mean dollar volume >= $20M, active and inactive, ~1,840-1,950 per day); bars end at 15:59 (no closing auction).

design.registered_at: 2026-10-24, before any option or stock outcome is fetched or read
design.question: Does unusually call-heavy option volume in a stock on day t predict its next-day intraday return (09:45 -> close) in the cross-section? Literature: Pan & Poteshman (2006, RFS) - option volume put/call ratios predict next-day/next-week stock returns (strongest with buyer-initiated opening trades, which free data cannot sign); Johnson & So (2012, JFE) - a HIGH option-to-stock volume ratio predicts LOWER returns. Long-only desk: the primary buys call-heavy names.
design.prior: LOW-MEDIUM (~15%): the published PCR effect uses signed opening volume (not available); unsigned volume carries a weaker version; option-heavy names may instead underperform (Johnson & So), which the information cell reports.
design.universe: Each month: the 100 US common stocks with the highest prior-month median dollar volume among the gap-down study's ever-liquid list (active + inactive, raw close >= $10 on the prior day) that have listed options (a non-empty contract list). Stock daily bars fetched on the data-only account (RAW) 2024-01-01 .. 2026-10-15 except 2026-01-14 .. 04-24.
design.option_data: For each universe name and day t: contracts with expiration in (t, t + 45 calendar days] and strike within +/-15% of the stock's day-t RAW close (contract lists via the contracts endpoint, active and inactive); their daily option bars (data-only account). CV = summed call volume, PV = summed put volume, TV = CV + PV. A name-day with TV < 100 contracts is ineligible (counted).
design.signal: CS = CV / TV (call share). Z = (CS_t - mean of CS over the name's previous 20 trading days) / their SD (needs >= 15 days with TV >= 100; SD > 0). Known after the day-t close (daily option bars complete).
design.trade: Day t+1: buy the 09:45 SIP 1-minute bar open (RAW, >= $10), sell at the last close at or before 15:59 (C2). LONG = the top DECILE of Z among that day's eligible names (>= 30 eligible, else the day is skipped). Cost 5 bp round trip binding (3, 10, 20 printed).
design.primary: LIFT = top-decile mean return minus the equal-weight mean of all eligible names over the same window (day t+1); per day; day-equal; day-clustered t, plus a two-way (day x name) clustered t of the trade-level excess.
design.halves: A = signal days 2024-03-01 .. 2025-06-30; B = 2025-07-01 .. 2026-01-12 and 2026-05-26 .. 2026-10-14 (every look-back and the next-day trade stay outside the held-out window 2026-01-14 .. 04-24). Confirmation: the held-out window, fetched only after a PASS.
design.pass: In BOTH halves: LIFT >= +5 bp with day-clustered t >= 2.0 AND two-way t >= 2.0, AND top-decile mean net (after 5 bp) > 0. Batch-robust label: t >= 2.84 in both halves (11-study batch).
design.fail: t <= -2 in a half, or both halves' 97.5% upper bound of LIFT < +5 bp. Otherwise UNDERPOWERED.
design.power: Outcome-blind count step: eligible name-days, long trades and days per half; MDE = (2.0 + 0.84) x SD(day placebo LIFT) / sqrt(days), placebo = a seeded random decile of the same size (seed 'options-flow-placebo'); floors >= 300 long trades and >= 20 days per half and MDE <= 5 bp, else UNDERPOWERED with no outcome read; --score refuses unless both halves meet the floors.
information_only: Johnson-So: top decile of option-to-stock volume ratio (TV x 100 / stock share volume) LIFT (expected negative)
volume surge: TV >= 2x its 20-day mean, top-decile Z among those
next-day close -> close (t close to t+1 close) LIFT
design.c4: Every fetch logs failures and 429-dropped symbols; a half with any unrecovered gap or a truncated page is refused; per-name-month contract lists and bar files are written only when complete.
design.budget: Probe estimate before the full fetch: pages per name-month for contracts and bars on 5 seeded name-months; the fetch runs only if the estimate is <= 8 hours at <= 150 requests/min, else the universe is cut to the top 50 names by the same rank (rule fixed here).
declared: volume is unsigned (no buyer/seller or opening/closing classification on free data)
Alpaca option data feed as served (OPRA-derived historical bars); its fidelity vs OPRA is not independently verified
the strike/expiry filter (+/-15%, 45 days) is fixed, not tuned
design.no_retuning: Universe size, 45-day / 15% filters, 100-contract floor, 20-day Z, top decile, 09:45 entry, cost, halves and floors are fixed.
